text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it like reorganizing a messy closet: you rearrange things so they are easier to find, but you don’t throw away your clothes or change their purpose. The main goal is to make the code more readable and easier to maintain. This often involves breaking long functions into smaller pieces, renaming confusing variables, or removing duplicate logic. Over time, skipping refactoring creates technical debt—a kind of “interest” you pay later in bugs and slow development. By regularly cleaning up your code, you save time in the long run and make it easier for others to work with.
